newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary c.bank cuts rates as sees inflaton decline.
newsitem.headline: Hungary c.bank cuts rates as sees inflaton decline.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said on Friday that it cut four of its repo rates by 50 basis points as it expected inflation to continue to fall and it also wanted to smooth out the downward interest rate curve.
"We wish to make the interest curve smoother," the NBH said in a statement.

Earlier on Friday the NBH announced that it cut the overnight and the one-week repo rates to 26.25 percent, the one-month reverse repo rate to 20.75 percent and the one-week reverse repo rate to 20.25 percent.
The NBH left the overnight reverse repo rate unchanged at 17.25 percent, the six-month deposit rate remained 21 percent and the 12-month deposit rate 20.50 percent.
"The NBH continues to expect inflation to decline," the central bank said in a statement. "The NBH believes the interest rates over one-month maturity are appropriate.
Inflation ran at 18.6 percent in April and the government expects it to go down to between 16 and 17 percent by December.
The NBh said said that the 50 basis point cut in one-month and shorter than one-month repo rates smoothed out the central bank interest rate curve.
"And this also matches the decline in yields, which is expected to come at a moderate pace," it added.
